metadata.title: [Perf][SM75] Turing tensor-core paths for block-FP8 QPN8 and the grouped skinny MoE; bound the MoE grid
metadata.body:
Update 2026-10-28: rebased onto main c59b3c4cb. The seven commits apply unchanged (git range-diff shows no difference), and #1279, #1280 and #1282 stack on these same commits again. Test Plan files on this head, one process per file, on a Quadro RTX 8000 / Tesla V100: test_skinny_sm70_moe.py 103 / 89 passed, test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py 113 passed / 95 passed and 1 failed, test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py 24, test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py 55, test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py 34 and test_sm70_path_explanations.py 29 passed on both cards. The failures (test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py 168 and test_sm70_native_policy.py 1 on both cards, test_volta_medium_prefill_keeps_original_turbomind_output[64] on the V100) are the same test IDs on main c59b3c4cb, as described under Known failures below. pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD on this head: every hook passes except check-layering, which now reports vllm/config/speculative.py (model coupling 142 -> 144) next to vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (platform coupling 37 -> 39); main c59b3c4cb reports the same two counts, so this PR adds none. pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual: passed.

## Purpose

Turing (SM75) runs the SM70 kernel family through binary compatibility with sm_70 code, and the hand kernels use Volta's mma.m8n8k4, which Turing executes at half its tensor rate. This PR gives the family native Turing paths where they pay off and bounds the grouped MoE grid on both cards. Volta numerics change in one place: the grouped skinny MoE now splits the w13 reduction over 8 instead of 16 warps, so Volta MoE output is no longer bit-identical to main (group 2). Seven commits in two groups:

1. Block-FP8 QPN8 linears on Turing (3e4b5a8b4, 28ecc05ba) and an occupancy split-K for the M <= 8 launch (b08b9f2ac).
   - A new m16n8k8 GEMM decodes and block-scales the packed QPN8 codes once per CTA while staging them in shared memory (bit-identical to the dense reconstruction), reads both operands through ldmatrix, rasterises row tiles in groups and splits K across CTAs with a fixed-order FP32 reduction. No second weight layout.
   - Turing runs M = 9..512 through it; the M decision stays inside the opaque op as before. M <= 8 keeps the packed m8n8k4 GEMM, which in CUDA graphs was faster on 10 of 13 DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes. Above M = 512 the dense prefill stays. can_implement requires the Turing GEMM's op by the capability of the worker's own device, not device 0. Volta's routes are unchanged. The route is now chosen from the capability of the weight's own device (it was the current device).
   - Split-K of the M <= 8 GEMM: on Turing (1024 threads per SM) a split-16 CTA fills half an SM, so N = 5120 spills a second, almost empty wave; split 8 fits it into one wave. The fitted split applies only to the M <= 8 launch, where it was measured. FP8QPN8LinearState keeps the table split (split_k) and the fitted one (decode_split_k); the opaque turing_fp8_qpn8_linear op takes both and picks by its own input rows, so torch.compile cannot fold the choice into one constant for every M. The per-tensor M16/M32 bodies keep the table split (their native M = 17..32 candidate takes split-K 12 or 16), and fp8_qpn8_launch_config(k) returns the table split. Volta keeps its table. A split-K 32 rule for grids with no more CTAs than SMs was measured on DeepSeek-V4 and not adopted (see the message of b08b9f2ac).
2. Grouped skinny MoE (6a4512994, 67e2b8a6a, d7c0ab302, 001b73e3e).
   - The grid spans min(routing slots, experts) rows instead of one row per slot; a batch never has more groups than experts. Bit-identical.
   - On SM75 (the backend admits capability 7.0 and 7.5 only), expert weights are packed at load in the m16n8k8 fragment order (a pure permutation, same size, no second copy; each layer lives on one card), and a new kernel uses the weights as the 16-row A operand and the expert rows as the B operand. Volta keeps m8n8k4. The decoded weights equal the m8n8k4 path bit for bit; only the tensor core's summation order differs.
   - Volta takes over the tile structure found on Turing: two 32-column tiles per CTA share each staged activation fragment, and both GEMMs prefer eight split-K warps (16 or 10 only where 8 does not divide K/16). The tiles alone change no bit, but w13 moves from split 16 (main) to split 8, which regroups its FP32 reduction; w2 already used 8. The two-accumulator variant had no caller and leaves the kernel and the op signature.
   - mma_fragments_sm70.cuh holds the e2m1 decoder (derived from TurboMind's cvt_f16x8_e2m1, Apache-2.0), the m16n8k8 MMA and ldmatrix once. It replaces the e2m1 decoder copies in nvfp4_qpn4_sm70.cu and skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu, and the new fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75.cu takes its MMA and ldmatrix from it. Below SM75 the m16n8k8 and ldmatrix helpers trap, so a binary that lacks the sm_75 image fails loudly instead of returning wrong values.
   - The skewed-routing case (a few experts with hundreds of rows, others with a handful) is now part of the dispatch test.

Build: the SM70 family keeps main's architecture lists (sm_70; Turing runs it through binary compatibility). Only the two sources with Turing instructions get sm_75 code: fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75.cu builds for 7.5 only (3e4b5a8b4), and skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu gets an sm_75 image next to its sm_70 one (67e2b8a6a). TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST stays 7.0: listing 7.5 there would turn the Marlin build mixed and drop the SM70 Marlin kernels. Building the whole family for 7.0 and 7.5 was tried in our fork and dropped, because it gave no measurable gain (Test Result).

Not a duplicate. Open PRs on the same files or the same problem, checked with gh and with git merge-tree of every open PR against main and against this branch (rechecked on main 899e9ed33 for the PRs named here):
- #1069 and #1157 (kezboard233) also address block-scaled QPN8 FP8 at M 9..32, on SM70: #1069 chunks those rows through the M <= 8 kernels, #1157 adds a native M = 17..32 kernel. Both change the native dispatch op fp8_qpn8_dispatch_sm70_out. This PR only moves two decode helpers out of that file into a shared header and does not change the dispatch; its block-FP8 kernel (QPN8Fp8BlockScaledMMLinearKernel) calls the packed GEMM, the new Turing GEMM and the prefill ops directly. They target Volta decode with several 8-token verify rows; the new GEMM runs on Turing only, for M 9..512. No textual conflict with either.
- #1030 (split-K 4, 6, 9, 12 and 18 and K % 32 for DeepSeek-V4.1 MoE shapes), #1031 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on V100) and #1243 (stacked on #1031) carry the same change to skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu and skinny_sm70_moe.py; it adds split specialisations and does not change fragment order, grid or tiles. All three already conflict with main 899e9ed33 (in 1, 13 and 14 files). This branch adds conflicts in those two files to each; whichever lands second has to re-add the new splits on the new tile structure (this branch also drops the two-accumulator variant their check still names).
- #822 (QPN2 activation packing through per-engine policy, already conflicting with main) gains a conflict in tests/quantization/test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py, where both add tests.
- #1216 (mine, two-rank host all-reduce) edits the same CMake block; git merge-tree merges CMakeLists.txt cleanly with this branch, and its two remaining conflicts (runtime_reference.md, kernel.py) exist against main already.
- Searches of open PRs for m16n8k8, QPN8, "QPN8 Turing", "Turing tensor", sm_75, SM75, "skinny MoE" and split-K find, besides these, our own Turing PRs for other kernels and PRs in other areas (#953 and #1021 among the QPN8 hits); none changes these kernels or routes.

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and measurements below.

## Test Plan

Native build of this branch in place (MAX_JOBS=4, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.0; only fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75.cu and skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu get sm_75 code), then cuobjdump --list-elf vllm/_C.abi3.so for the sm_70 and sm_75 images.

Kernel and selection tests, one pytest process per file, on a Quadro RTX 8000 (SM75) and on a Tesla V100 (SM70):
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py
python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_skinny_sm70_moe.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py

Policy, route and explanation contracts from the development guide, one process per file:
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_sm70_native_policy.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_sm70_path_explanations.py
On main 899e9ed33: python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category moe --output moe-main.json and python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category fp8 --output fp8-main.json; on this branch: python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category moe --check moe-main.json and python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category fp8 --check fp8-main.json

pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: default enabled, chosen per layer from the capability of its own device (Turing GEMM, m16n8k8 MoE order and split-K rule on 7.5; Volta MoE tiles on 7.0; grid bound on both); no switch.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none for this change. The model runs used DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MXFP4 experts, block-FP8 linears) PP=5 over the five cards (first and last stage on an RTX 8000), DSpark with 5 speculative tokens, --max-num-batched-tokens 512, --dtype half; Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (per-tensor FP8 attention projections) and Qwen3.8-27B FP8 (128x128 block scales), each TP=2 on the two RTX 8000 with MTP (3 speculative tokens), --max-num-batched-tokens 2048, --dtype float16; all with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 and NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: fp8 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash), auto (both Qwen3.8-27B checkpoints).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: kernel microbenchmarks compare each commit's kernel source with its parent (numbers from the commit messages). Model A/B runs used fork builds of github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, named per A/B below. This branch carries the same changes rebased onto main 899e9ed33 plus the later changes described in Purpose (split-K scoped to M <= 8 and chosen inside the op, can_implement on the worker's own device, traps below SM75, sm_75 code only for the two m16n8k8 sources); it is built and unit-tested, not booted with a full model.
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: in each model A/B the changed arm ran the same entry with PYTHONPATH on its fork source tree and its own compile cache; both arms used the stock Triton 3.6.0 of the environment (the bundled run named under Test Result also used a patched Triton). Unit tests: in-place build, no overlays.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: the changed DeepSeek-V4-Flash boots logged "Block FP8 QPN8 on SM75: M=1..8 uses the packed decode GEMM, M=9..512 the tensor-core GEMM on the packed codes, larger M the FP16 prefill." (a load-time route declaration, not a per-call trace); the Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 boots selected TuringQpn8Fp8LinearKernel for the FP8 projections. Speed and quality: Test Result.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: selection stays in QPN8Fp8BlockScaledMMLinearKernel, TuringQpn8Fp8LinearKernel and the skinny MoE backend. On SM75 the block-FP8 kernel also requires fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75_out and otherwise reports it as a missing native operator.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: commands in Test Plan; no intentional changed rows (the selected kernels stay the same; the new routes are chosen inside the native op by M and at weight load by the device's capability). Result below.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

Kernel microbenchmarks (from the commit messages; CUDA graphs, time per call, lower is better):
- QPN8 block-FP8 GEMM on a Quadro RTX 8000 (3e4b5a8b4; 20 calls per CUDA graph, replays interleaved, 13 DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes): at M = 16..64 0.16-0.60x the time of the previous path (whole-weight reconstruction + cuBLAS). At M = 1..8 it took 1.01-1.28x the time of the packed GEMM on 10 of 13 shapes and 0.78-1.02x on the other three, so M <= 8 stays on the packed GEMM.
- Block scale read with the codes (28ecc05ba, RTX 8000): BM128 tiles at M 128..512 7-12 % faster, BM16/32/64 within 2 %; outputs bitwise equal in 840 tile and split configurations on the Qwen3.8-27B TP2 shapes.
- M <= 8 split-K on Turing (b08b9f2ac, RTX 8000, M = 1..8): o_proj/out_proj (K 3072) 0.78-0.90 and down_proj (K 8704) 0.73-0.87 of the split-16 time. On a V100 split 8 took 1.18-1.24x on spilling grids, so Volta keeps its table.
- Skinny MoE grid bound (6a4512994; sm_70 code on both cards, synthetic weights, uniform routing): DeepSeek-V4 shapes, 512 tokens (E256 top-6): RTX 8000 w13 7070 -> 6506 us, w2 3546 -> 3250 us; V100 w13 5524 -> 5004 us, w2 3004 -> 2442 us; 6-token decode unchanged; bit-identical.
- Skinny MoE m16n8k8 on a Quadro RTX 8000 (67e2b8a6a, same checkpoint weights in both orders): DeepSeek-V4 512 tokens w13 6555 -> 4303 us, w2 3271 -> 2238 us; GLM-5.3 512 tokens w13 8566 -> 5316 us, w2 4205 -> 2760 us; decode (4-6 tokens) -1.3 % .. +1.0 %. The m8n8k4 order of the new source is bit-identical to the previous kernel; the m16n8k8 order stays within 6.3e-4 of the output maximum and matches the fp32 reference as closely.
- Skinny MoE tiles on a Tesla V100 (d7c0ab302): DeepSeek-V4 512 tokens w13 4979 -> 4374 us, w2 2441 -> 2395 us; GLM-5.3 512 tokens w13 6878 -> 5954 us, w2 3567 -> 3218 us; decode (4-6 tokens) 0.80-0.97x.

Model A/B/A/B on fork builds (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM; 3 Tesla V100 + 2 Quadro RTX 8000 on PCIe, no P2P). The two builds of each A/B differ only by the commits named; both carry other fork changes over 1Cat main. Each series: one uncounted cold boot of the changed build, then reference, changed, reference, changed. tok/s higher is better, ms and s lower is better. Texts: greedy output of three fixed prompts and eight quality answers per boot, compared byte for byte.
- QPN8 Turing GEMM with this PR's routing (3e4b5a8b4 + 28ecc05ba; reference 23e34b03c, changed 4da0bcfa4), DeepSeek-V4-Flash: prefill at 32,668 / 178,480 / 287,039 tokens 14.76-14.77 -> 14.63-14.66 s, 113.40-113.41 -> 112.71-112.74 s, 223.59 -> 222.42 s (0.5-0.8 % lower); decode step 62-63 / 65 / 70 -> 62 / 65 / 70 ms (prose / code / edit). The prefill GEMM rounds differently, so greedy output differs on 2 of 3 prompts and 7 of 8 quality answers differ between the arms (identical within each arm across all boots); all were read and judged correct and equivalent. Because the texts differ, per-prompt tok/s are not comparable: prose 48.3 -> 47.2-47.3, code 73.5-73.6 -> 67.6-67.7 (4.78 -> 4.41 accepted tokens per round at the same step time), edit 80.7-81.2 -> 80.4-80.9. Sampled draft acceptance (temperature 1.0, top_k 40, top_p 1.0, min_p 0.1, fixed seeds, one boot per arm) was mixed: prose 35.4 -> 37.1 %, English 38.2 -> 37.6 %, code 72.0 -> 71.6 %, edit 93.5 -> 93.2 %.
- Intermediate state, not this PR's routing: Qwen3.8-27B FP8 with the new GEMM also at M = 1..8 (reference 23e34b03c, changed 7f343a791): decode 56.3-56.9 -> 56.9-57.4 tok/s (prose), 82.6-84.5 -> 83.2-85.1 (code), 86.9-87.0 -> 87.4-87.6 (edit), step 45-47 -> 45-46 ms; at 184,134 tokens of context 67.1 -> 66.8-66.9 ms per step; prefill unchanged (184,134 tokens 351.73-351.74 -> 351.62-351.66 s); greedy output and the eight quality answers byte-identical to the reference in both counted boots. This PR sends M <= 8 back to the packed GEMM; the final routing was not re-measured on this checkpoint.
- Occupancy split-K (b08b9f2ac; reference 23e34b03c, changed 6c0ef8efb = the GEMM commits plus the rule; this checkpoint has no block-FP8 layers, its per-tensor FP8 projections see only the rule), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4: decode prose 74.2-74.5 -> 75.6-75.7 tok/s, code 114.3-114.9 -> 116.4-116.9, edit 118.8-119.1 -> 120.6-121.0 (arm means +1.75 / +1.79 / +1.60 %), step 33-34 -> 32-33 ms; at 184,134 tokens 54.6-54.7 -> 54.2 ms per step; prefill unchanged (249,992 tokens 565.86 -> 565.82-566.04 s); greedy output and eight answers byte-identical in all boots. The measured build also used split 8 for the per-tensor M 9..32 bodies; this PR keeps the table split there (as on main), which the decode measurement (M = 4) does not exercise. The build carried sm_70 code only (see the sm_75 A/B below).
- Grid bound (6a4512994; reference e1cb50fd9, changed 79e07bfef, the grid commit only), DeepSeek-V4-Flash: two A/B/A/B series on the same entry with the same reference arm (fork build 4da0bcfa4, within 0.1 % between the series); comparing their changed arms: prefill at 32,668 / 178,480 / 287,039 tokens 12.94 -> 12.32-12.33 s, 82.14-82.20 -> 79.00-79.03 s, 149.72-149.73 -> 144.25-144.76 s (4.75 / 3.84 / 3.49 % lower); decode step 61 / 63 / 69 ms in both builds (46.9-47.0 / 71.6-71.8 / 82.3-82.8 tok/s before, 46.8-47.0 / 71.6-71.7 / 82.2-82.8 after); greedy output and eight answers byte-identical between the two builds' boots.
- sm_75 images for the whole family, tried in our fork and dropped. DeepSeek-V4-Flash (fork builds: reference 79e07bfef, changed 5028a3fc4 = the family built for 7.0 and 7.5; this build still ran the m8n8k4 MoE kernel on Turing): prefill at 32,668 / 178,480 / 287,039 tokens 12.33 -> 12.30 s, 79.11-79.12 -> 78.92-78.97 s, 144.52-144.56 -> 144.18-144.47 s (0.15-0.24 % lower); decode step 61 / 63-64 / 69 ms -> 61 / 63-64 / 68 ms; greedy output and eight answers byte-identical in all five boots. Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, A/B/A/B of the fork's production build with the whole family for 7.0 and 7.5 (0181fdc6c) against the same source with this PR's lists (c168acab6), two boots per arm, whole family -> this PR's lists: prefill at 8,490 tokens 5.60-5.64 -> 5.61-5.65 s; short decode 78.2 / 70.0 / 77.2 -> 77.8 / 70.5 / 77.8 tok/s (three prompts, each the same in both boots of an arm); decode step at 33,208 / 184,134 / 249,992 tokens of context 35.5 / 52.8 / 60.7-60.8 -> 35.2 / 52.5 / 60.4 ms; first token at 184,134 / 249,992 tokens 175.32-175.66 / 270.41-270.78 -> 175.09-175.28 / 269.71-270.65 s; memory per card the same. Seven of eight quality answers are byte-identical to the reference; the eighth differs in wording with the same result, as it also does between boots of the production build. The extra images bring no gain; an earlier single boot that had pointed to a 1 % decode loss on this checkpoint was not confirmed.
- Volta MoE tiles (d7c0ab302) and m16n8k8 MoE (67e2b8a6a): no isolated model A/B. In the fork both reached a full model only bundled with eleven other commits and a patched Triton (reference 79e07bfef, changed 7b8fb5387, DeepSeek-V4-Flash); there the texts differ from the reference, and the eight quality answers of both counted changed boots were read and judged correct. The speed of that bundle cannot be attributed to these commits and is not reported here.

Unit tests on this branch, native build in place (_C carries 72 sm_70 and 2 sm_75 cubins), one process per file:
- Quadro RTX 8000: test_skinny_sm70_moe.py 103 passed, 33 skipped; test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py 113 passed, 10 skipped; test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py 34 passed; test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py 24 passed; test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py 55 passed; test_sm70_path_explanations.py 29 passed; test_sm70_native_policy.py 90 passed, 1 failed; test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py 55 passed, 168 failed.
- Tesla V100: test_skinny_sm70_moe.py 89 passed, 47 skipped; test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py 95 passed, 27 skipped, 1 failed (test_volta_medium_prefill_keeps_original_turbomind_output[64]); test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py 34 passed; test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py 24 passed; test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py 55 passed; test_sm70_path_explanations.py 29 passed; test_sm70_native_policy.py 90 passed, 1 failed; test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py 55 passed, 168 failed.
- test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py also passes without a visible GPU (24 passed).
- Route snapshots, main 899e9ed33 -> this branch: moe 168 configurations, fp8 324 configurations, no changed route.
The failures in test_sm70_native_policy.py and test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py are the same test IDs on main 899e9ed33 (in-place build of main; the tree also carried the Python-only #1272, which touches neither file): of the 168 fp4 mainflow failures, 118 raise NameError for _DFLASH_NVFP4_TRACE_ARMED, 49 AttributeError ('Module' object has no attribute 'top_k') and one expects a ValueError that is not raised. On main 6a143197e the same file failed 119 times.

Known failures to read these results against:
- tests/quantization/test_sm70_native_policy.py::test_packaged_native_policy_schemas_parse_before_build also fails on main 899e9ed33: gguf_grouped_prefill_gemm_sm70_out takes native_policy but is missing from CONFIGURED_OPERATORS. #1273 (open) adds it. This branch lists its own new op, fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75_out.
- On the V100, test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py::test_volta_medium_prefill_keeps_original_turbomind_output compares two TurboMind calls bit for bit. With fp8_tune_small_shapes unset (the default), the runtime tuning times candidates for each new small shape and can pick different tiles for the two calls; #1187 proposes turning that default off. On an earlier build of this branch, two runs of this test alone failed 2 and then 1 of its 2 cases, and three runs with the tuning switched off passed. That the failure is independent of this PR is so far shown by code reading only: the branch does not change the Volta TurboMind path the test compares. discussion.title: [Perf][SM75] Turing tensor-core paths for block-FP8 QPN8 and the grouped skinny MoE; bound the MoE grid
discussion.body:
Update 2026-10-28: rebased onto main c59b3c4cb. The seven commits apply unchanged (git range-diff shows no difference), and #1279, #1280 and #1282 stack on these same commits again. Test Plan files on this head, one process per file, on a Quadro RTX 8000 / Tesla V100: test_skinny_sm70_moe.py 103 / 89 passed, test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py 113 passed / 95 passed and 1 failed, test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py 24, test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py 55, test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py 34 and test_sm70_path_explanations.py 29 passed on both cards. The failures (test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py 168 and test_sm70_native_policy.py 1 on both cards, test_volta_medium_prefill_keeps_original_turbomind_output[64] on the V100) are the same test IDs on main c59b3c4cb, as described under Known failures below. pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD on this head: every hook passes except check-layering, which now reports vllm/config/speculative.py (model coupling 142 -> 144) next to vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (platform coupling 37 -> 39); main c59b3c4cb reports the same two counts, so this PR adds none. pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual: passed.

## Purpose

Turing (SM75) runs the SM70 kernel family through binary compatibility with sm_70 code, and the hand kernels use Volta's mma.m8n8k4, which Turing executes at half its tensor rate. This PR gives the family native Turing paths where they pay off and bounds the grouped MoE grid on both cards. Volta numerics change in one place: the grouped skinny MoE now splits the w13 reduction over 8 instead of 16 warps, so Volta MoE output is no longer bit-identical to main (group 2). Seven commits in two groups:

1. Block-FP8 QPN8 linears on Turing (3e4b5a8b4, 28ecc05ba) and an occupancy split-K for the M <= 8 launch (b08b9f2ac).
   - A new m16n8k8 GEMM decodes and block-scales the packed QPN8 codes once per CTA while staging them in shared memory (bit-identical to the dense reconstruction), reads both operands through ldmatrix, rasterises row tiles in groups and splits K across CTAs with a fixed-order FP32 reduction. No second weight layout.
   - Turing runs M = 9..512 through it; the M decision stays inside the opaque op as before. M <= 8 keeps the packed m8n8k4 GEMM, which in CUDA graphs was faster on 10 of 13 DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes. Above M = 512 the dense prefill stays. can_implement requires the Turing GEMM's op by the capability of the worker's own device, not device 0. Volta's routes are unchanged. The route is now chosen from the capability of the weight's own device (it was the current device).
   - Split-K of the M <= 8 GEMM: on Turing (1024 threads per SM) a split-16 CTA fills half an SM, so N = 5120 spills a second, almost empty wave; split 8 fits it into one wave. The fitted split applies only to the M <= 8 launch, where it was measured. FP8QPN8LinearState keeps the table split (split_k) and the fitted one (decode_split_k); the opaque turing_fp8_qpn8_linear op takes both and picks by its own input rows, so torch.compile cannot fold the choice into one constant for every M. The per-tensor M16/M32 bodies keep the table split (their native M = 17..32 candidate takes split-K 12 or 16), and fp8_qpn8_launch_config(k) returns the table split. Volta keeps its table. A split-K 32 rule for grids with no more CTAs than SMs was measured on DeepSeek-V4 and not adopted (see the message of b08b9f2ac).
2. Grouped skinny MoE (6a4512994, 67e2b8a6a, d7c0ab302, 001b73e3e).
   - The grid spans min(routing slots, experts) rows instead of one row per slot; a batch never has more groups than experts. Bit-identical.
   - On SM75 (the backend admits capability 7.0 and 7.5 only), expert weights are packed at load in the m16n8k8 fragment order (a pure permutation, same size, no second copy; each layer lives on one card), and a new kernel uses the weights as the 16-row A operand and the expert rows as the B operand. Volta keeps m8n8k4. The decoded weights equal the m8n8k4 path bit for bit; only the tensor core's summation order differs.
   - Volta takes over the tile structure found on Turing: two 32-column tiles per CTA share each staged activation fragment, and both GEMMs prefer eight split-K warps (16 or 10 only where 8 does not divide K/16). The tiles alone change no bit, but w13 moves from split 16 (main) to split 8, which regroups its FP32 reduction; w2 already used 8. The two-accumulator variant had no caller and leaves the kernel and the op signature.
   - mma_fragments_sm70.cuh holds the e2m1 decoder (derived from TurboMind's cvt_f16x8_e2m1, Apache-2.0), the m16n8k8 MMA and ldmatrix once. It replaces the e2m1 decoder copies in nvfp4_qpn4_sm70.cu and skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu, and the new fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75.cu takes its MMA and ldmatrix from it. Below SM75 the m16n8k8 and ldmatrix helpers trap, so a binary that lacks the sm_75 image fails loudly instead of returning wrong values.
   - The skewed-routing case (a few experts with hundreds of rows, others with a handful) is now part of the dispatch test.

Build: the SM70 family keeps main's architecture lists (sm_70; Turing runs it through binary compatibility). Only the two sources with Turing instructions get sm_75 code: fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75.cu builds for 7.5 only (3e4b5a8b4), and skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu gets an sm_75 image next to its sm_70 one (67e2b8a6a). TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST stays 7.0: listing 7.5 there would turn the Marlin build mixed and drop the SM70 Marlin kernels. Building the whole family for 7.0 and 7.5 was tried in our fork and dropped, because it gave no measurable gain (Test Result).

Not a duplicate. Open PRs on the same files or the same problem, checked with gh and with git merge-tree of every open PR against main and against this branch (rechecked on main 899e9ed33 for the PRs named here):
- #1069 and #1157 (kezboard233) also address block-scaled QPN8 FP8 at M 9..32, on SM70: #1069 chunks those rows through the M <= 8 kernels, #1157 adds a native M = 17..32 kernel. Both change the native dispatch op fp8_qpn8_dispatch_sm70_out. This PR only moves two decode helpers out of that file into a shared header and does not change the dispatch; its block-FP8 kernel (QPN8Fp8BlockScaledMMLinearKernel) calls the packed GEMM, the new Turing GEMM and the prefill ops directly. They target Volta decode with several 8-token verify rows; the new GEMM runs on Turing only, for M 9..512. No textual conflict with either.
- #1030 (split-K 4, 6, 9, 12 and 18 and K % 32 for DeepSeek-V4.1 MoE shapes), #1031 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on V100) and #1243 (stacked on #1031) carry the same change to skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu and skinny_sm70_moe.py; it adds split specialisations and does not change fragment order, grid or tiles. All three already conflict with main 899e9ed33 (in 1, 13 and 14 files). This branch adds conflicts in those two files to each; whichever lands second has to re-add the new splits on the new tile structure (this branch also drops the two-accumulator variant their check still names).
- #822 (QPN2 activation packing through per-engine policy, already conflicting with main) gains a conflict in tests/quantization/test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py, where both add tests.
- #1216 (mine, two-rank host all-reduce) edits the same CMake block; git merge-tree merges CMakeLists.txt cleanly with this branch, and its two remaining conflicts (runtime_reference.md, kernel.py) exist against main already.
- Searches of open PRs for m16n8k8, QPN8, "QPN8 Turing", "Turing tensor", sm_75, SM75, "skinny MoE" and split-K find, besides these, our own Turing PRs for other kernels and PRs in other areas (#953 and #1021 among the QPN8 hits); none changes these kernels or routes.

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and measurements below.

## Test Plan

Native build of this branch in place (MAX_JOBS=4, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.0; only fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75.cu and skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu get sm_75 code), then cuobjdump --list-elf vllm/_C.abi3.so for the sm_70 and sm_75 images.

Kernel and selection tests, one pytest process per file, on a Quadro RTX 8000 (SM75) and on a Tesla V100 (SM70):
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py
python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_skinny_sm70_moe.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py

Policy, route and explanation contracts from the development guide, one process per file:
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_sm70_native_policy.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_sm70_path_explanations.py
On main 899e9ed33: python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category moe --output moe-main.json and python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category fp8 --output fp8-main.json; on this branch: python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category moe --check moe-main.json and python tools/sm70_route_snapshot.py --category fp8 --check fp8-main.json

pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| QPN8Fp8BlockScaledMMLinearKernel on SM75 | block FP8 (128x128 scales, QPN8 codes) | M 9..512, decided inside the opaque op, CUDA graphs | new m16n8k8 GEMM fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75_out | executed: test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py on RTX 8000; measured: CUDA graphs (3e4b5a8b4, 28ecc05ba), DeepSeek-V4-Flash A/B | SM7.5 cards other than the RTX 8000; Qwen3.8-27B FP8 with this routing (only an earlier routing was measured) |
| same on SM75 | block FP8 | M <= 8; M > 512 | packed m8n8k4 GEMM (split-K below); dense FP16 prefill as on main | executed: test_turing_decode_keeps_the_packed_gemm (bit-identical to the packed GEMM) | none |
| same on SM70 | block FP8 | all M | routes and split-K table unchanged | executed: same file on V100 | none |
| M <= 8 split-K | QPN8 FP8, block and per-tensor | Turing; grid spills a second wave that holds fewer than half the SMs; K/16 divisible by 8 | split-K 8 instead of 16 for the M <= 8 launch; per-tensor M16/M32 bodies keep the table split; Volta keeps the table | executed: test_qpn8_split_k_follows_device_occupancy, test_qpn8_per_tensor_launch_config_is_the_table_split, test_qpn8_per_tensor_op_picks_the_split_by_m; measured: CUDA graphs (b08b9f2ac), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 A/B | the scoping to M <= 8 (per-tensor M 9..32 back on the table split, as on main) was not measured on a model |
| skinny grouped MoE on SM75 | NVFP4, MXFP4 | prefill and decode; the backend admits capability 7.0 and 7.5 only | m16n8k8 fragment order packed at load, m16n8k8 kernel | executed: test_skinny_sm70_moe.py on RTX 8000 (both orders, skewed routing); measured: CUDA graphs (67e2b8a6a) | no isolated model A/B |
| skinny grouped MoE on SM70 | NVFP4, MXFP4 | prefill and decode | m8n8k4 order, two column tiles, split-K 8 (w13 was 16): output not bit-identical to main | executed: same file on V100 against the fp32 reference; measured: CUDA graphs (d7c0ab302) | no isolated model A/B on Volta |
| skinny MoE grid bound | NVFP4, MXFP4 | both cards, both fragment orders | grid rows min(slots, experts) | executed: same file on both cards; measured: CUDA graphs (6a4512994), DeepSeek-V4-Flash A/B, bit-identical | none |
| build | n/a | TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.0 | SM70 family sm_70 as on main; skinny_moe_qpn_sm70.cu sm_70 and sm_75; fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75.cu sm_75 only; Marlin unchanged | static: cuobjdump (Test Result); measured: model A/B against a whole-family sm_75 build | builds with other arch lists |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: default enabled, chosen per layer from the capability of its own device (Turing GEMM, m16n8k8 MoE order and split-K rule on 7.5; Volta MoE tiles on 7.0; grid bound on both); no switch.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none for this change. The model runs used DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MXFP4 experts, block-FP8 linears) PP=5 over the five cards (first and last stage on an RTX 8000), DSpark with 5 speculative tokens, --max-num-batched-tokens 512, --dtype half; Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (per-tensor FP8 attention projections) and Qwen3.8-27B FP8 (128x128 block scales), each TP=2 on the two RTX 8000 with MTP (3 speculative tokens), --max-num-batched-tokens 2048, --dtype float16; all with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 and NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: fp8 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash), auto (both Qwen3.8-27B checkpoints).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: kernel microbenchmarks compare each commit's kernel source with its parent (numbers from the commit messages). Model A/B runs used fork builds of github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, named per A/B below. This branch carries the same changes rebased onto main 899e9ed33 plus the later changes described in Purpose (split-K scoped to M <= 8 and chosen inside the op, can_implement on the worker's own device, traps below SM75, sm_75 code only for the two m16n8k8 sources); it is built and unit-tested, not booted with a full model.
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: in each model A/B the changed arm ran the same entry with PYTHONPATH on its fork source tree and its own compile cache; both arms used the stock Triton 3.6.0 of the environment (the bundled run named under Test Result also used a patched Triton). Unit tests: in-place build, no overlays.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: the changed DeepSeek-V4-Flash boots logged "Block FP8 QPN8 on SM75: M=1..8 uses the packed decode GEMM, M=9..512 the tensor-core GEMM on the packed codes, larger M the FP16 prefill." (a load-time route declaration, not a per-call trace); the Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 boots selected TuringQpn8Fp8LinearKernel for the FP8 projections. Speed and quality: Test Result.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: selection stays in QPN8Fp8BlockScaledMMLinearKernel, TuringQpn8Fp8LinearKernel and the skinny MoE backend. On SM75 the block-FP8 kernel also requires fp8_qpn8_mma_sm75_out and otherwise reports it as a missing native operator.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: commands in Test Plan; no intentional changed rows (the selected kernels stay the same; the new routes are chosen inside the native op by M and at weight load by the device's capability). Result below.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

Kernel microbenchmarks (from the commit messages; CUDA graphs, time per call, lower is better):
- QPN8 block-FP8 GEMM on a Quadro RTX 8000 (3e4b5a8b4; 20 calls per CUDA graph, replays interleaved, 13 DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes): at M = 16..64 0.16-0.60x the time of the previous path (whole-weight reconstruction + cuBLAS). At M = 1..8 it took 1.01-1.28x the time of the packed GEMM on 10 of 13 shapes and 0.78-1.02x on the other three, so M <= 8 stays on the packed GEMM.
- Block scale read with the codes (28ecc05ba, RTX 8000): BM128 tiles at M 128..512 7-12 % faster, BM16/32/64 within 2 %; outputs bitwise equal in 840 tile and split configurations on the Qwen3.8-27B TP2 shapes.
- M <= 8 split-K on Turing (b08b9f2ac, RTX 8000, M = 1..8): o_proj/out_proj (K 3072) 0.78-0.90 and down_proj (K 8704) 0.73-0.87 of the split-16 time. On a V100 split 8 took 1.18-1.24x on spilling grids, so Volta keeps its table.
- Skinny MoE grid bound (6a4512994; sm_70 code on both cards, synthetic weights, uniform routing): DeepSeek-V4 shapes, 512 tokens (E256 top-6): RTX 8000 w13 7070 -> 6506 us, w2 3546 -> 3250 us; V100 w13 5524 -> 5004 us, w2 3004 -> 2442 us; 6-token decode unchanged; bit-identical.
- Skinny MoE m16n8k8 on a Quadro RTX 8000 (67e2b8a6a, same checkpoint weights in both orders): DeepSeek-V4 512 tokens w13 6555 -> 4303 us, w2 3271 -> 2238 us; GLM-5.3 512 tokens w13 8566 -> 5316 us, w2 4205 -> 2760 us; decode (4-6 tokens) -1.3 % .. +1.0 %. The m8n8k4 order of the new source is bit-identical to the previous kernel; the m16n8k8 order stays within 6.3e-4 of the output maximum and matches the fp32 reference as closely.
- Skinny MoE tiles on a Tesla V100 (d7c0ab302): DeepSeek-V4 512 tokens w13 4979 -> 4374 us, w2 2441 -> 2395 us; GLM-5.3 512 tokens w13 6878 -> 5954 us, w2 3567 -> 3218 us; decode (4-6 tokens) 0.80-0.97x.

Model A/B/A/B on fork builds (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM; 3 Tesla V100 + 2 Quadro RTX 8000 on PCIe, no P2P). The two builds of each A/B differ only by the commits named; both carry other fork changes over 1Cat main. Each series: one uncounted cold boot of the changed build, then reference, changed, reference, changed. tok/s higher is better, ms and s lower is better. Texts: greedy output of three fixed prompts and eight quality answers per boot, compared byte for byte.
- QPN8 Turing GEMM with this PR's routing (3e4b5a8b4 + 28ecc05ba; reference 23e34b03c, changed 4da0bcfa4), DeepSeek-V4-Flash: prefill at 32,668 / 178,480 / 287,039 tokens 14.76-14.77 -> 14.63-14.66 s, 113.40-113.41 -> 112.71-112.74 s, 223.59 -> 222.42 s (0.5-0.8 % lower); decode step 62-63 / 65 / 70 -> 62 / 65 / 70 ms (prose / code / edit). The prefill GEMM rounds differently, so greedy output differs on 2 of 3 prompts and 7 of 8 quality answers differ between the arms (identical within each arm across all boots); all were read and judged correct and equivalent. Because the texts differ, per-prompt tok/s are not comparable: prose 48.3 -> 47.2-47.3, code 73.5-73.6 -> 67.6-67.7 (4.78 -> 4.41 accepted tokens per round at the same step time), edit 80.7-81.2 -> 80.4-80.9. Sampled draft acceptance (temperature 1.0, top_k 40, top_p 1.0, min_p 0.1, fixed seeds, one boot per arm) was mixed: prose 35.4 -> 37.1 %, English 38.2 -> 37.6 %, code 72.0 -> 71.6 %, edit 93.5 -> 93.2 %.
- Intermediate state, not this PR's routing: Qwen3.8-27B FP8 with the new GEMM also at M = 1..8 (reference 23e34b03c, changed 7f343a791): decode 56.3-56.9 -> 56.9-57.4 tok/s (prose), 82.6-84.5 -> 83.2-85.1 (code), 86.9-87.0 -> 87.4-87.6 (edit), step 45-47 -> 45-46 ms; at 184,134 tokens of context 67.1 -> 66.8-66.9 ms per step; prefill unchanged (184,134 tokens 351.73-351.74 -> 351.62-351.66 s); greedy output and the eight quality answers byte-identical to the reference in both counted boots. This PR sends M <= 8 back to the packed GEMM; the final routing was not re-measured on this checkpoint.
- Occupancy split-K (b08b9f2ac; reference 23e34b03c, changed 6c0ef8efb = the GEMM commits plus the rule; this checkpoint has no block-FP8 layers, its per-tensor FP8 projections see only the rule), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4: decode prose 74.2-74.5 -> 75.6-75.7 tok/s, code 114.3-114.9 -> 116.4-116.9, edit 118.8-119.1 -> 120.6-121.0 (arm means +1.75 / +1.79 / +1.60 %), step 33-34 -> 32-33 ms; at 184,134 tokens 54.6-54.7 -> 54.2 ms per step; prefill unchanged (249,992 tokens 565.86 -> 565.82-566.04 s); greedy output and eight answers byte-identical in all boots. The measured build also used split 8 for the per-tensor M 9..32 bodies; this PR keeps the table split there (as on main), which the decode measurement (M = 4) does not exercise. The build carried sm_70 code only (see the sm_75 A/B below).
- Grid bound (6a4512994; reference e1cb50fd9, changed 79e07bfef, the grid commit only), DeepSeek-V4-Flash: two A/B/A/B series on the same entry with the same reference arm (fork build 4da0bcfa4, within 0.1 % between the series); comparing their changed arms: prefill at 32,668 / 178,480 / 287,039 tokens 12.94 -> 12.32-12.33 s, 82.14-82.20 -> 79.00-79.03 s, 149.72-149.73 -> 144.25-144.76 s (4.75 / 3.84 / 3.49 % lower); decode step 61 / 63 / 69 ms in both builds (46.9-47.0 / 71.6-71.8 / 82.3-82.8 tok/s before, 46.8-47.0 / 71.6-71.7 / 82.2-82.8 after); greedy output and eight answers byte-identical between the two builds' boots.
- sm_75 images for the whole family, tried in our fork and dropped. DeepSeek-V4-Flash (fork builds: reference 79e07bfef, changed 5028a3fc4 = the family built for 7.0 and 7.5; this build still ran the m8n8k4 MoE kernel on Turing): prefill at 32,668 / 178,480 / 287,039 tokens 12.33 -> 12.30 s, 79.11-79.12 -> 78.92-78.97 s, 144.52-144.56 -> 144.18-144.47 s (0.15-0.24 % lower); decode step 61 / 63-64 / 69 ms -> 61 / 63-64 / 68 ms; greedy output and eight answers byte-identical in all five boots. Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, A/B/A/B of the fork's production build with the whole family for 7.0 and 7.5 (0181fdc6c) against the same source with this PR's lists (c168acab6), two boots per arm, whole family -> this PR's lists: prefill at 8,490 tokens 5.60-5.64 -> 5.61-5.65 s; short decode 78.2 / 70.0 / 77.2 -> 77.8 / 70.5 / 77.8 tok/s (three prompts, each the same in both boots of an arm); decode step at 33,208 / 184,134 / 249,992 tokens of context 35.5 / 52.8 / 60.7-60.8 -> 35.2 / 52.5 / 60.4 ms; first token at 184,134 / 249,992 tokens 175.32-175.66 / 270.41-270.78 -> 175.09-175.28 / 269.71-270.65 s; memory per card the same. Seven of eight quality answers are byte-identical to the reference; the eighth differs in wording with the same result, as it also does between boots of the production build. The extra images bring no gain; an earlier single boot that had pointed to a 1 % decode loss on this checkpoint was not confirmed.
- Volta MoE tiles (d7c0ab302) and m16n8k8 MoE (67e2b8a6a): no isolated model A/B. In the fork both reached a full model only bundled with eleven other commits and a patched Triton (reference 79e07bfef, changed 7b8fb5387, DeepSeek-V4-Flash); there the texts differ from the reference, and the eight quality answers of both counted changed boots were read and judged correct. The speed of that bundle cannot be attributed to these commits and is not reported here.

Unit tests on this branch, native build in place (_C carries 72 sm_70 and 2 sm_75 cubins), one process per file:
- Quadro RTX 8000: test_skinny_sm70_moe.py 103 passed, 33 skipped; test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py 113 passed, 10 skipped; test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py 34 passed; test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py 24 passed; test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py 55 passed; test_sm70_path_explanations.py 29 passed; test_sm70_native_policy.py 90 passed, 1 failed; test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py 55 passed, 168 failed.
- Tesla V100: test_skinny_sm70_moe.py 89 passed, 47 skipped; test_sm70_qpn8_block_fp8.py 95 passed, 27 skipped, 1 failed (test_volta_medium_prefill_keeps_original_turbomind_output[64]); test_turing_qpn_kernel_selection.py 34 passed; test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py 24 passed; test_sm70_moe_mainflow.py 55 passed; test_sm70_path_explanations.py 29 passed; test_sm70_native_policy.py 90 passed, 1 failed; test_sm70_fp4_mainflow.py 55 passed, 168 failed.
- test_block_fp8_qpn8_capabilities.py also passes without a visible GPU (24 passed).
